Implement the following plan:

# Fix: E2E Triage Output Not Showing in GitHub Actions Job Summary

## Context

The triage workflow runs successfully and produces good output (visible in the "Run triage" step logs and in the uploaded artifact). But the "Summarize triage output" step writes to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and nothing renders in the GitHub Actions UI summary tab.

**Root cause:** `claude -p` outputs text with ANSI escape codes and terminal control sequences (cursor movements, color codes like `[36;1m`, `[?2026h`). When `tee` writes this to the triage log file, the raw bytes go into `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, which expects clean markdown. GitHub silently drops or corrupts the summary when it contains control characters.

## Fix

### 1. Strip ANSI/control codes from the triage log before writing to summary

**File:** `.github/workflows/e2e-triage.yml` (Summarize triage output step)

In the summary step, strip ANSI escape codes when writing to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`:

```bash
# Strip ANSI escape codes and control characters before writing to summary
sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]//g; s/\x1b\[[?][0-9]*[a-zA-Z]//g' "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
```

### 2. Use `--output-format text` in claude invocation

**File:** `scripts/run-e2e-triage.sh`

Add `--output-format text` to the `claude` command to get cleaner output without tool-use formatting:

```bash
claude \
  --plugin-dir .claude/plugins/e2e \
  --output-format text \
  --allowedTools "Read" "Grep" "Glob" \
  -p "$triage_args" \
  2>&1 | tee "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE"
```

### 3. Also strip in the tee pipeline as belt-and-suspenders

**File:** `scripts/run-e2e-triage.sh`

Pipe through `sed` to strip ANSI before `tee` so the file itself is clean:

```bash
claude ... -p "$triage_args" 2>&1 \
  | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]//g; s/\x1b\[[?][0-9]*[a-zA-Z]//g' \
  | tee "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE"
```

## Files to modify

1. `scripts/run-e2e-triage.sh` — add `--output-format text` and strip ANSI in pipeline
2. `.github/workflows/e2e-triage.yml` — strip ANSI when writing to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (defense in depth)

## Verification

1. Push changes
2. Run: `gh workflow run e2e-triage.yml --ref alisha/e2e-triage-ci-job -f run_url="https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/23314820664"`
3. Check the job's Summary tab in GitHub Actions UI — should show the triage report as rendered markdown

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
ANSI escape codes (like `\x1b[36;1m` for cyan bold) are emitted by CLI tools that detect a TTY. When piped through `tee` to a file, these raw bytes persist. GitHub Actions' `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` expects clean markdown — control characters cause silent rendering failures. The fix uses two layers: `--output-format text` reduces noise at the source, and `sed` stripping provides defense-in-depth.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

#!/usr/bin/env bash

set -euo pipefail

: "${RUN_URL:?RUN_URL is required}"
: "${E2E_AGENT:?E2E_AGENT is required}"
: "${TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE:?TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE is required}"

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE")"

# Download artifacts before invoking Claude so it only needs read-only access
artifact_path="$(scripts/download-e2e-artifacts.sh "$RUN_URL")"

triage_args="/e2e:triage-ci ${artifact_path} --agent ${E2E_AGENT}"
if [ -n "${TRIAGE_SHA:-}" ]; then
  triage_args="${triage_args} --sha ${TRIAGE_SHA}"
fi

claude \
  --plugin-dir .claude/plugins/e2e \
  --allowedTools \
    "Read" \
    "Grep" \
    "Glob" \
  -p "$triage_args" \
  2>&1 | tee "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE"

name: E2E Triage

on:
  repository_dispatch:
    types:
      - slack_e2e_triage_requested
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      run_url:
        description: GitHub Actions run URL to triage
        required: true
        type: string
      sha:
        description: Commit SHA (auto-detected from run if omitted)
        required: false
        type: string
      failed_agents:
        description: Comma-separated list of failed agents (auto-detected from run if omitted)
        required: false
        type: string
      slack_channel:
        description: Slack channel ID for the originating thread
        required: false
        type: string
      slack_thread_ts:
        description: Slack thread timestamp for replies
        required: false
        type: string

permissions:
  actions: read
  contents: read

jobs:
  matrix-setup:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      agents: ${{ steps.set.outputs.agents }}
      run_url: ${{ steps.set.outputs.run_url }}
      sha: ${{ steps.set.outputs.sha }}
      slack_channel: ${{ steps.set.outputs.slack_channel }}
      slack_thread_ts: ${{ steps.set.outputs.slack_thread_ts }}
    steps:
      - name: Validate payload and build matrix
        id: set
        shell: bash
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REPO_NAME: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_URL_INPUT: ${{ inputs.run_url }}
          SHA_INPUT: ${{ inputs.sha }}
          FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT: ${{ inputs.failed_agents }}
          SLACK_CHANNEL_INPUT: ${{ inputs.slack_channel }}
          SLACK_THREAD_TS_INPUT: ${{ inputs.slack_thread_ts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          csv_to_json() {
            printf '%s' "$1" | jq -R -s -c 'split(",") | map(gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$"; "")) | map(select(length > 0))'
          }

          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            run_url="$RUN_URL_INPUT"
            sha="${SHA_INPUT:-}"
            slack_channel="${SLACK_CHANNEL_INPUT:-}"
            slack_thread_ts="${SLACK_THREAD_TS_INPUT:-}"

            # Derive missing values from run URL via GitHub API
            if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ -z "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT" ]; then
              run_id=$(echo "$run_url" | grep -oE '/runs/[0-9]+' | grep -oE '[0-9]+')
              if [ -z "$run_id" ]; then
                echo "Could not extract run ID from run_url: $run_url" >&2
                exit 1
              fi
              run_data=$(gh run view "$run_id" --repo "$REPO_NAME" --json headSha,jobs)
              if [ -z "$sha" ]; then
                sha=$(echo "$run_data" | jq -r '.headSha')
              fi
              if [ -z "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT" ]; then
                agents_json=$(echo "$run_data" | jq -c '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure") | .name | capture("\\((?<agent>[^)]+)\\)") | .agent]')
              fi
            fi

            if [ -n "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT" ]; then
              agents_json="$(csv_to_json "$FAILED_AGENTS_INPUT")"
            fi
          else
            trigger_text="$(jq -r '.client_payload.trigger_text // empty' "$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH")"
            repo="$(jq -r '.client_payload.repo // empty' "$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH")"
            branch="$(jq -r '.client_payload.branch // empty' "$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH")"
            run_url="$(jq -r '.client_payload.run_url // empty' "$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH")"
            sha="$(jq -r '.client_payload.sha // empty' "$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH")"
            slack_channel="$(jq -r '.client_payload.slack_channel // empty' "$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH")"

          fi

        with:

          path: e2e-triage-artifacts/
          retention-days: 7

set -euo pipefail

: "${RUN_URL:?RUN_URL is required}"
: "${E2E_AGENT:?E2E_AGENT is required}"
: "${TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE:?TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE is required}"

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE")"

# Download artifacts before invoking Claude so it only needs read-only access
artifact_path="$(scripts/download-e2e-artifacts.sh "$RUN_URL")"

triage_args="/e2e:triage-ci ${artifact_path} --agent ${E2E_AGENT}"
if [ -n "${TRIAGE_SHA:-}" ]; then
  triage_args="${triage_args} --sha ${TRIAGE_SHA}"
fi

claude \
  --plugin-dir .claude/plugins/e2e \
  --output-format text \
  --allowedTools \
    "Read" \
    "Grep" \
    "Glob" \
  -p "$triage_args" \
  2>&1 | sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]//g; s/\x1b\[[?][0-9]*[a-zA-Z]//g' \
  | tee "$TRIAGE_OUTPUT_FILE"

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**Why two layers of stripping?** `--output-format text` tells the Claude CLI to skip tool-use JSON formatting and reduce decorative output, but it doesn't guarantee zero escape codes — the underlying terminal detection may still emit some. The `sed` pipeline is the actual guarantee. Having it in both the script (clean file on disk) and the workflow (clean summary) follows defense-in-depth: if either layer fails or is bypassed, the other catches it.

**The sed pattern explained:** `\x1b\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]` matches standard CSI sequences (colors, bold, etc.) and `\x1b\[[?][0-9]*[a-zA-Z]` matches private-mode sequences (like `?2026h` for synchronized output). Together they cover the escape codes that Claude CLI and terminal emulators produce.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Summary of changes:**

1. **`scripts/run-e2e-triage.sh`** — Added `--output-format text` to get cleaner Claude output, and piped through `sed` to strip any remaining ANSI escape codes before writing to the log file.

2. **`.github/workflows/e2e-triage.yml`** — Replaced `cat` with `sed` (same ANSI-stripping pattern) when writing to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, as defense-in-depth.
